findings.invariant: Pilot output must remain inside a newly created directory.
findings.counterexample: Pre-create receipts/mandate.json or runtime/fixed-append.txt as a symlink to another host file.
findings.affected_claim: No host-path escape.
findings.correction: Require a new output root and use exclusive no-follow file opens.

findings.invariant: Coverage counts only exact, unique, role-accepted observation projections.
findings.counterexample: A duplicate signed decision or an ID-matching receipt with a different operation hash covers the observation.
findings.affected_claim: Per-anchor coverage detects direct bypasses.
findings.correction: Use decision_event_id and exact seven-field projection equality; invalidate every duplicate.

findings.invariant: Pilot credentials must not appear in argv or ambient subprocess state.
findings.counterexample: The MCP signer seed was supplied as --signer-seed and the child inherited the parent environment.
findings.affected_claim: No credential or environment access in the fixed MCP boundary.
findings.correction: Transfer the seed through bootstrap stdin and construct a minimal child environment.

findings.invariant: Pilot JSON input must be bounded and unambiguous.
findings.counterexample: Duplicate members select the last value; a newline-free stdio request is buffered before its size is checked.
findings.affected_claim: Fixed, bounded HTTP and MCP input surface.
findings.correction: Use strict duplicate-aware JSON parsing and bounded line reads.

findings.invariant: Every required failed verification dimension must exit nonzero.
findings.counterexample: FAILED coverage, witness inclusion, or correction status returned exit 0.
findings.affected_claim: Exit 1 on integrity or required proof failure.
findings.correction: Include coverage, witness, and correction dimensions in the exit-code hard set.

findings.invariant: Boolean values must never satisfy integer fields.
findings.counterexample: schema_version=true compared equal to 1 and receipted=true compared equal to 1.
findings.affected_claim: Closed machine-readable coverage and witness schemas.
findings.correction: Reject bool before every integer comparison.

findings.invariant: Witness inclusion and witnessed_at require a signed checkpoint bound to an externally accepted witness.
findings.counterexample: An unsigned included-hash list produced inclusion and witnessed-time claims.
findings.affected_claim: Witness inclusion and four-label temporal evidence.
findings.correction: Bind checkpoint fields by hash and domain-separated witness-checkpoint proof; require external role and root trust.

findings.invariant: A receipt signer must match both packet-core role declaration and external context.
findings.counterexample: A context-accepted key absent from packet-core signed a timeline receipt.
findings.affected_claim: Issuer authenticity and role topology.
findings.correction: Bind every receipt role to the exact packet-core issuer and recompute mandate role_issuers.

findings.invariant: Duplicate accepted projections cannot cover an observation.
findings.counterexample: The second projection silently overwrote the first.
findings.affected_claim: Coverage is fail-closed.
findings.correction: Remove all duplicate candidates from the covering set and report them invalid.

findings.invariant: Effect and evidence commitments remain separate.
findings.counterexample: capability.observe projected effect_hash into evidence_hash.
findings.affected_claim: Exact denominator projection.
findings.correction: Carry and project a distinct evidence_hash.

findings.invariant: Issuer-policy failures must affect issuer_authenticity without being mislabeled as cryptographic signature failure.
findings.counterexample: A receipt issuer rejection left issuer_authenticity VERIFIED.
findings.affected_claim: Multidimensional verification.
findings.correction: Track role/issuer-policy failure separately.

findings.invariant: Receipt-directory coverage cannot follow symlinks or consume unbounded aggregate input.
findings.counterexample: A symlink root or member was followed by is_dir/read_bytes; many individually valid-size files had no aggregate cap.
findings.affected_claim: Strict byte-boundary coverage ingestion.
findings.correction: Reject symlink roots/members, read regular files without following links, and cap files and aggregate bytes.

findings.invariant: Timeline attestations must bind the exact receipt file bytes carried by the packet.
findings.counterexample: Appending whitespace to a semantically unchanged receipt preserved the attestation and previously verified.
findings.affected_claim: Packet archive byte integrity and public byte parity.
findings.correction: Add signed byte_length and sha256 fields to every timeline entry and verify before receipt semantics.

findings.invariant: Standalone checkers must enforce every closed action field, role, handoff, mandate, and correction commitment enforced by the kernel.
findings.counterexample: A re-signed capability.decide decision=ALLOW or handoff with an arbitrary coverage_hash was accepted by an earlier standalone checker.
findings.affected_claim: Python, Node, and kernel expected-verdict interoperability.
findings.correction: Mirror closed action semantics, mandate role issuers, handoff prefix/coverage/parent commitments, typed correction resolution, and counterparty role constraints.

findings.invariant: A verification-context issuer cannot occupy more than one incident role.
findings.counterexample: The publisher DID was added to the accepted gateway set and an earlier standalone parser accepted the context.
findings.affected_claim: External role topology.
findings.correction: Reject cross-role issuer collisions in Python and Node context parsing.

findings.invariant: Packet file reads must not follow a member swapped to a symlink after metadata inspection.
findings.counterexample: Earlier checkers used lstat followed by a path-based read, leaving a check/read race.
findings.affected_claim: No host-path escape.
findings.correction: Python uses descriptor-relative no-follow traversal; Node uses O_NOFOLLOW descriptor reads plus inode and size checks.

findings.invariant: Only the affected-party role may issue a counterparty_confirmed statement.
findings.counterexample: A reviewer-signed statement was re-signed with epistemic_status=counterparty_confirmed.
findings.affected_claim: Party statement provenance.
findings.correction: Freeze counterparty_confirmed to issuer_role=affected_party.

findings.invariant: Corrections resolve within their declared kind and cannot select a future or wrapper-self target.
findings.counterexample: A statement correction was re-labeled packet while retaining statement hashes; wrapper canonical_hash(core) was accepted as a packet replacement shortcut.
findings.affected_claim: Typed, append-only corrections.
findings.correction: Resolve statement refs to prior named statements and packet refs to distinct released conforming packet-core artifacts; key forks by kind and supersedes ref.

findings.invariant: Once an observation ID is duplicated, later copies cannot re-enter the eligible set.
findings.counterexample: Three identical receipts removed the second copy but re-admitted the third.
findings.affected_claim: Duplicate projections cannot cover an observation.
findings.correction: Persist a duplicate-ID tombstone independently of the current eligible map.

findings.invariant: Public packet roots contain only members declared by packet-core.
findings.counterexample: A generated expected-verdict sidecar inside each packet root made downloaded directories fail strict parsing as undeclared.
findings.affected_claim: Browser/download/standalone packet interoperability.
findings.correction: Publish report and context as hashed sidecars outside packet roots and limit public_files to actual packet members.

findings.invariant: A packet publisher alone cannot shorten an effect denominator and erase a bypass.
findings.counterexample: Remove the bypass row, update coverage/artifact commitments, and re-sign the handoff, witness checkpoint, and publish receipt; all three verifiers report clean 1/1.
findings.affected_claim: Per-anchor coverage exposes direct bypasses.
findings.correction: Require a distinct earlier accepted topology-constrained incident.statement whose closed claim and sole self_asserted evidence bind the exact denominator artifact digest.

findings.invariant: A represented protocol cannot omit its entire decision or effect coverage phase.
findings.counterexample: Remove the effect denominator and matching coverage reference, then re-sign packet publication.
findings.affected_claim: Per-anchor coverage exposes boundary bypasses.
findings.correction: Require exactly one decision denominator and one effect denominator, plus matching coverage reports, for every represented protocol.

findings.invariant: A downstream receipt must use the exact accepted prior mandate for its run and policy.
findings.counterexample: A gateway re-signs a capability decision with a different run_id or policy_digest while retaining a resolving mandate_ref.
findings.affected_claim: Authority binding.
findings.correction: Require an earlier accepted mandate, exact run and policy bindings, inclusive decision claimed-time bounds, and exact observe parent mandate/protocol fields.

findings.invariant: A handoff must bind the complete ordered prior record.
findings.counterexample: Re-sign a handoff after omitting or reordering a statement or parent, or include a statement created after the handoff.
findings.affected_claim: Timeline and handoff integrity.
findings.correction: Require statement_refs to equal ordered named prior statements and parent_refs to equal the complete ordered prior timeline.

findings.invariant: A redaction reviewer must bind the exact redaction transformation record.
findings.counterexample: The publisher changes a release digest in a redaction record and republishes without reviewer participation.
findings.affected_claim: Redaction binding.
findings.correction: Add a distinct released redaction record and require an accepted reviewer statement with a closed claim and sole self_asserted reference to its exact bytes.

findings.invariant: Actor-authenticated claimed_at cannot supply witness or external-anchor time.
findings.counterexample: Re-sign a receipt with a future claimed_at, or carry anchored_before in the team witness checkpoint without separate anchor proof.
findings.affected_claim: Four distinct temporal labels.
findings.correction: Populate received_at and witnessed_at only from accepted witness intake; reject anchored_before without separate external proof.

findings.invariant: Fixed pilot clients must reject every non-canonical external destination before connection.
findings.counterexample: Call the low-level HTTP helper with an HTTPS, DNS, IPv6, credential-bearing, query-bearing, or alternate-path URL.
findings.affected_claim: Localhost-only pilot execution.
findings.correction: Validate literal loopback scheme, host, port, path, userinfo, query, and fragment before the opener; bind MCP to a validated port and literal loopback.

findings.invariant: A failed semantic dimension must suppress every conclusion that depends on it.
findings.counterexample: Earlier semantic timeline, coverage, redaction, witness, and correction failures exposed only the raw failed dimension.
findings.affected_claim: Multidimensional fail-closed verification.
findings.correction: Emit deterministic suppression labels for reliance, content, timeline/lineage, coverage, redaction/disclosure, witness time, and correction resolution.

findings.invariant: Only a receipt that passes both its exact-byte timeline commitment and accepted attestation verification may reduce an uncovered denominator observation.
findings.counterexample: Append one trailing whitespace byte to a valid decision receipt; the standalone checkers reported the timeline mismatch but still counted its parsed projection as covering the event.
findings.affected_claim: Exact-byte, fail-closed per-anchor coverage parity across the kernel, Python checker, and Node checker.
findings.correction: Keep byte-mismatched receipts in the invalid-receipt report while excluding them from the accepted projection map; preserve valid cryptographic proof dimensions for a byte-only mismatch.

findings.invariant: Receipt integrity, content signature, authority binding, occurrence binding, and issuer policy are separate verification dimensions.
findings.counterexample: The standalone checkers mapped every receipt error to failed signature and occurrence status, so authorization-purpose transplants, occurrence-purpose transplants, missing signatures, byte-only mismatches, and a corrupted stored content hash did not match the kernel.
findings.affected_claim: Multidimensional Python/Node/kernel verdict parity.
findings.correction: Verify content, occurrence, and authorization proofs independently over recomputed hashes: authorization failures affect authority without poisoning a valid occurrence proof; occurrence failures affect occurrence and dependent authority; missing content signatures fail the dependent proof set and issuer binding; byte-only and stored-hash failures do not alter otherwise valid proof dimensions.

findings.invariant: A conforming controlled denominator or coverage artifact is unavailable evidence, not failed evidence.
findings.counterexample: Set a coverage artifact to controlled with path=null and remove its public file; Python marked coverage FAILED and Node attempted to dereference the null path and exposed raw exception text.
findings.affected_claim: Availability is distinct from integrity and controlled evidence can remain non-public.
findings.correction: Return the affected anchor and aggregate coverage as NOT_COMPUTED with the frozen unavailable reason, preserve recomputed counts when only the declared report is controlled, list the artifact as unavailable, and exit zero. Apply the same semantics to controlled denominators.

findings.invariant: Every claimed or witnessed time accepted by the profile is a valid RFC 3339 UTC instant ending in Z.
findings.counterexample: Permissive datetime parsing accepted offset-form or otherwise non-frozen claimed_at, received_at, and witnessed_at values; an invalid late correction could enter claimed temporal evidence.
findings.affected_claim: Four-label temporal evidence and correction ordering parity.
findings.correction: Use one strict UTC instant validator for every timeline and publish claimed_at, mandate validity endpoints, and witness received_at/witnessed_at; invalid receipts remain excluded from claimed temporal evidence.

findings.invariant: Profile evidence grounding and ordered evidence commitments are role-sensitive and closed.
findings.counterexample: Re-signed decisions and observations could substitute counterparty, third-party, or execution-verified grounding, or reorder evidence hashes, while the standalone checkers still accepted the receipt.
findings.affected_claim: Grounding labels and exact decision/effect evidence projection.
findings.correction: Require self_asserted decision and gateway/boundary observation evidence, counterparty_signed target observations, exact evidence hash order, no third_party_anchored claim by team-controlled roles, and recomputation-prefixed names for execution_verified evidence.

findings.invariant: A standalone checker must validate the closed ActionReceipt v0.4 base record before accepting stored hashes or proofs.
findings.counterexample: A coherently re-signed receipt with a non-canonical event_id, malformed diagnostic/evidence/convention/stake/base field, unsupported executable convention form, unknown nested remedy field, whitespace-only semantic forum endpoint, or unknown nested v0.3 delegation/checkpoint/proof member reached proof acceptance in the standalone implementations.
findings.affected_claim: Independent ActionReceipt v0.4 interoperability without importing Bulla.
findings.correction: Validate canonical lowercase UUIDv4 event_id, strict diagnostic and evidence-reference shapes, grounding classes, the complete closed jsonschema+quantum/1 executable form, convention pins and nonblank closed forums, reserved-null stake, claimed_at, every closed nested mandate/remedy/retention object, and source-parser-exact delegation grant/checkpoint/proof wire shapes before hash and proof acceptance; keep independent delegation semantics out of receipt_integrity to preserve kernel parity.
findings.test: ActionReceipt v0.4 malformed UUID, diagnostic, evidence, convention, stake, and base-field parity regressions; test_signed_publish_receipt_nested_shapes_fail_closed_with_checker_parity; test_signed_delegation_nested_shapes_fail_closed_with_checker_parity

findings.invariant: Statement, correction, and witness references are closed structural packet-core commitments bound to the correct timeline row or artifact role.
findings.counterexample: Nested ambient fields, mismatched path/hash pairs, wrong action types, duplicate references, and witness artifacts with the wrong role were accepted until later semantic verification or accepted outright.
findings.affected_claim: Strict packet-core ingestion and append-only statement/correction/witness topology.
findings.correction: Close all three reference object types, enforce uniqueness, safe paths and hashes, exact path/hash/action binding, witness artifact existence/role, and recursively apply the same complete component validator to released predecessor packet-core artifacts.
findings.test: test_nested_reference_unknown_fields_are_structurally_malformed; statement/correction path-hash-action and witness artifact binding regressions

findings.invariant: Denominator and coverage topology is completely validated during structural ingestion, independently of artifact availability.
findings.counterexample: Unsupported provenance, missing or wrong-role artifacts, reused denominator artifacts or checkpoints, denominator/coverage aliasing, and non-attestation coverage depth degraded to semantic exit 1 or leaked implementation exceptions.
findings.affected_claim: Malformed packet-core inputs exit 2 and cannot introduce unknown coverage provenance or topology.
findings.correction: Validate artifact existence, required roles, non-reuse and distinctness, the frozen provenance enum, unique checkpoints, exact anchor/phase/protocol types, matching decision/effect phase pairs, and minimum_verification_depth=attestation before semantic verification.

findings.invariant: A live incident-profile receipt must have one cross-runtime verification meaning and cannot depend on a host-language regular-expression dialect.
findings.counterexample: A coherently signed executable convention using the Python named-group pattern '(?P<packet>a)' was accepted by the kernel and Python checker but rejected by the Node checker.
findings.affected_claim: Cross-language verification parity for glyph.agent-incident-packet/0.1-draft.
findings.correction: Narrow the experimental profile so every live timeline and publish receipt requires conventions=[] after ordinary ActionReceipt v0.4 structural validation. Nonempty conventions are a profile receipt failure. Normative ActionReceipt v0.4 remains unchanged; convention-bearing historical records may be carried only as opaque released evidence artifacts and are outside live timeline verification.

findings.invariant: Every released member declared by a deterministic or public packet is present in a clean repository checkout.
findings.counterexample: The repository-wide coverage ignore rule omitted all eight normative and public coverage report files from Git while local generators still saw them, so every clean CI checkout rejected the packets as incomplete.
findings.affected_claim: Clean-checkout packet verification, public byte parity, and generated evidence reproducibility.
findings.correction: Unignore only the incident packet coverage directories and commit all four normative plus four public coverage reports.
findings.test: clean git-archive generator and Python/Node standalone verification; CI incident packet jobs

findings.invariant: The strict parser uses descriptor-relative traversal only on hosts that can open and enumerate directory descriptors.
findings.counterexample: Windows exposed the Python dir_fd capability sets but could not open the packet root as a directory descriptor, causing every standalone packet verification to fail before parsing.
findings.affected_claim: macOS and Windows standalone checker portability.
findings.correction: Require a POSIX host with a real O_DIRECTORY flag before selecting descriptor-relative traversal and use the documented strict path fallback elsewhere in both the kernel and standalone Python checker.

findings.invariant: Generated capability-status provenance names the exact tracked incident verifier source bytes.
findings.counterexample: The Windows parser portability correction changed incident_packet.py after the prior status generation, leaving sources.json pinned to the earlier source digest and failing clean-checkout status verification.
findings.affected_claim: Generated experimental maturity and evidence provenance are current at the reviewed commit.
findings.correction: Regenerate capability status after the parser correction and require the existing root --check gate in both workspace and clean archive review.

findings.invariant: Fallback traversal rejects Windows junctions and other filesystem reparse points before reading packet descendants.
findings.counterexample: On Windows, a declared packet directory could be replaced by an NTFS junction to an external directory; Path.is_symlink and os.walk(..., followlinks=False) did not guarantee rejection.
findings.affected_claim: Strict path-escape rejection on Windows fallback hosts.
findings.correction: Reject FILE_ATTRIBUTE_REPARSE_POINT metadata at the packet root and every fallback descendant in both Python implementations, retain the fallback concurrency limitation, and add a real Windows junction CI smoke.

findings.invariant: A CI smoke that expects verifier exit 2 must report success after confirming that exact exit code.
findings.counterexample: The Windows junction smoke asserted LASTEXITCODE=2 but left the expected nonzero code in PowerShell state, allowing the GitHub Actions wrapper to fail the successful rejection path.
findings.affected_claim: Windows standalone-checker junction rejection is enforced by a passing CI gate.
findings.correction: Capture the verifier exit code, assert that it equals 2, and explicitly exit 0 after the expected rejection is confirmed.
findings.test: Windows junction rejection smoke in incident-packet-standalone

findings.invariant: Witness inclusion and witness-derived temporal labels require a root accepted through the out-of-band verification context.
findings.counterexample: With trusted_witness_roots empty, all three verifiers reported witness_inclusion=VERIFIED and emitted received_at and witnessed_at even while reporting witness_root_trust=UNTRUSTED.
findings.affected_claim: Packet-carried trust material cannot authenticate witness inclusion or witness-derived time.
findings.correction: After complete structural, proof, issuer, and inclusion checks, an untrusted witness root now yields witness_inclusion=NOT_COMPUTED, witness_root_trust=UNTRUSTED, suppressed witness-derived temporal labels, and completed exit 0.

findings.invariant: Witness root trust remains an independent verdict when the witness proof, issuer, or inclusion check fails.
findings.counterexample: With trusted_witness_roots empty, bad-proof, wrong-issuer, and incomplete-inclusion mutations failed inclusion but incorrectly retained witness_root_trust=TRUSTED because exceptions bypassed the trust assignment.
findings.affected_claim: Multidimensional verification preserves both root distrust and the underlying witness-chain failure.
findings.correction: Set witness_root_trust=UNTRUSTED immediately after binding an absent root, continue every proof, issuer, inclusion, chronology, and anchor check, and downgrade only an otherwise verified inclusion to NOT_COMPUTED.

findings.invariant: Witness failures cannot be weakened by reference ordering or later artifact unavailability.
findings.counterexample: In a two-witness packet, ordering a failed proof before an unavailable controlled witness overwrote FAILED with UNAVAILABLE and changed exit 1 to exit 0; reversing only the references retained the hard failure.
findings.affected_claim: Witness verification is fail-closed and independent of packet member order.
findings.correction: After the third failed attempt on witness-verdict aggregation, narrow v0.1-draft to zero or one witness reference. Multiple witness references are structurally malformed and exit 2; multiple-witness aggregation remains explicitly unresolved.

findings.invariant: A protocol scope limit that causes structural rejection is disclosed on every owned public capability surface.
findings.counterexample: The v0.1 schema and verifiers rejected a second witness reference, but the experimental route, public claim, and capability-status source did not disclose the zero-or-one limit or unresolved aggregation.
findings.affected_claim: Technical evaluators can predict the browser and standalone verifier contract from the public experimental surface.
findings.correction: State the zero-or-one witness limit and unresolved multiple-witness aggregation on the route, public claim, and status source; freeze all three with the incident status gate and regenerate owned evidence.

findings.invariant: The canonical witness-cardinality limitation has identical claim strength across the route, public claim, and capability status.
findings.counterexample: The route and public claim said multiple-witness aggregation remains unresolved, but capability status only listed it among unestablished items and the gate accepted that weaker wording.
findings.affected_claim: All owned public surfaces state the same explicit protocol limitation.
findings.correction: Use one canonical two-sentence limitation verbatim on all three authoritative sources and make the incident status gate require the complete string on each.

findings.invariant: Packet-member byte reads preserve the exact on-disk byte length on every supported operating system.
findings.counterexample: A Windows clean checkout stored JSON with CRLF bytes; os.open used text mode, os.read translated CRLF to LF, and the standalone checker rejected packet-core.json because the translated read length differed from fstat size.
findings.affected_claim: The standalone checker verifies clean public packets on Windows and hashes exact retained bytes.
findings.correction: Open every regular packet member and newly written packet member with O_BINARY when available, retain no-follow flags, keep directory descriptors non-binary, and add a deterministic flag-and-fallback regression.
findings.test: test_packet_reader_regular_files_request_binary_mode; incident packet standalone Windows clean-checkout smoke

findings.invariant: Normative and public packet fixture bytes remain identical to their Git blobs on every supported checkout.
findings.counterexample: After binary reads were corrected, Windows Git checkout still converted canonical LF packet members to CRLF under text=auto, invalidating artifact, timeline, receipt, trace, redaction, witness, and coverage commitments.
findings.affected_claim: Clean-checkout verification and public packet byte parity are portable across Windows, macOS, and Linux.
findings.correction: Force eol=lf for the normative and public incident-packet trees only, and verify every tracked file under both prefixes resolves to the LF checkout attribute.
findings.test: test_incident_packet_checkout_attributes_force_lf; incident packet standalone Windows clean-checkout smoke

findings.invariant: The checkout-stability rule preserves opaque binary artifacts as well as current textual packet members.
findings.counterexample: Whole-tree text eol=lf fixed current JSON checkout bytes but would normalize CRLF inside a future opaque binary trace, corrupting its committed length and digest.
findings.affected_claim: Repository-hosted packet fixtures preserve arbitrary opaque artifact bytes across supported Git checkouts.
findings.correction: After the third failed attempt on exact-byte portability, narrow the fixture contract to Git-binary exact-byte trees with -text. Generators own canonical LF for textual members; Git performs no conversion for any packet member.
